summary: Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied at the University of Oslo, University of Copenhagen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held posts at Uppsala University and the University of Oslo (Professor from 1866).

Soraj Hongladarom works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He was an Erasmus Mundus exchange scholar at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (2008) and Linköping University, and held a post in philosophy at Chulalongkorn University (attested 2015).
Soshu Nishioka works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

Soshuku Shibatani, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied at Waseda University and Koyasan University (PhD 2013). He held posts at Sonoda Women's University, Junrei Henro Kenkyukai (2014), and Koyasan University (~2013, attested 2026).

Sotan Oka was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He was a professor (1899) and president (1918) at Komazawa University and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soyen Shaku was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Keio University and under several masters including Kosen Imakita. He served at Nagata Zendo (1890), Engaku-ji (1892), and as president of Hanazono University (1914-1917).

Sravana Borkataky-Varma studied at the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD). Working in Indology and religious studies, she taught at Rice, UNC Wilmington, University of Houston, University of Montana, Harvard, and held a fellowship at CSWR (~2021-2023).

Sravani Kanamarlapudi is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at the University of Washington (2019), under Richard G. Salomon, and as a PhD student at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Visva-Bharati University, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD 1963-1966), later serving as professor at Aligarh Muslim University (~1976-1997).

Sri Anirvan was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed his studies at the University of Dhaka (~1911-1914), Sanskrit College and University (~1914-1916), and the University of Calcutta (~1916-1918).
Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg (~1960-1967), where he later served as Privatdozent for Indology from 1973 to 1997.

Sriram Krishnan is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held academic posts at the University of Hyderabad, Central Sanskrit University, and the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad.

Srisa Chandra Vasu was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Government College University, Lahore (BA 1881). He served as a Vakil at Allahabad High Court (~1883), founded the Panini Office (1891), and was a Fellow at the University of Allahabad.

Stacey Van Vleet works in Tibetology, sinology, and history. She studied at the University of Colorado Boulder and Columbia University (PhD, attested 2006) under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, and held a post at Columbia (attested 2013).

Stanislas Julien, a sinologist and Indologist, studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat at the Collège de France. He held posts at the Institut de France, Bibliothèque nationale, INALCO, and was Chair of Chinese at the Collège de France (1832-1873).

Stanislav Grof studied at Charles University (~1950-1956). His career included posts at several psychiatric institutions, Johns Hopkins University (1967-1969), Maryland Psychiatric Research Center (1969-1973), Esalen Institute (1973-1987), and California Institute of Integral Studies (1994-2015).

Stanisław Schayer was an Indologist and philosopher. He became a professor at the University of Warsaw in 1922 and was a member of both the Warsaw Scientific Society (~1930-1941) and the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences (~1933-1941).
Stanley Abe is a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who held academic posts at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

Stanley Insler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Columbia, Yale (PhD 1963), and under Paul Thieme at Tübingen. He served as the Edward E. Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale University (~1980-2012).

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah studied under Bryce Ryan at the University of Ceylon, and earned his PhD at Cornell. He held academic posts at the University of Ceylon, Cambridge, Chicago, and served as professor of anthropology at Harvard (1976-2001).
